patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing progressive left leg pain for 2 months, with recent interference with sleep. The pain was initially treated as 'growing pains' with ibuprofen, without improvement. He recalls being hit in the thigh by a baseball one week before the onset of symptoms, resulting in redness and swelling that lasted several days.

Secondary_Symptoms: History of trauma to the leg

patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: No fever, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms reported.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive left leg pain and assess the pathological causes.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Hi doctor—I'm a 13-year-old boy, and over the past two months I've had progressively worsening pain in my left leg that’s been keeping me from sleeping. It started after I was hit in the thigh by a baseball about a week before it began, and I had redness and swelling for a few days after.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—it's mostly been the pain in my left leg rather than swelling in the joints themselves.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a feeling of itchiness anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any itching or a really scratchy feeling anywhere on my body.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Actually, I don’t have trouble lifting my arms over my head—my movement feels normal, and the main issue is the pain in my left leg.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any vision loss or changes at all.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever or felt extremely hot like that, and I haven’t been dizzy or very uncomfortable from being sick.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really—I haven’t been unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately. My main problem has been the worsening left leg pain that started after the baseball hit and has made it hard to sleep.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any burning or discomfort when I urinate. I haven’t noticed any urinary changes at all.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills or felt like I was shaking from being cold.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breast that feel fixed and don’t move when you touch them?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t noticed any lumps or masses anywhere on my chest, and I definitely don’t have fixed spots that don’t move when I touch them.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I haven’t really had pain or discomfort on my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips. The pain seems to be mainly in my left leg.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does that pain go away when you stop walking?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I haven’t noticed a specific calf pain when I walk that clearly goes away when I stop—I mostly feel the pain as a constant problem in my left leg, and it’s been getting worse over time.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, my urine hasn’t looked darker than usual, and I haven’t noticed any changes in my urination at all. The main thing is still the steadily worsening pain in my left leg that’s been interfering with my sleep.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, no—I can lift my arms up and move them across my body normally. The only problem I’m having is the progressively worsening pain in my left leg, and it’s been affecting my sleep.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you notice joint pain or stiffness after doing the same repetitive motion—like typing, lifting, or other repetitive tasks—for a while?
turns.patient_answer: “Not really, doctor. I don’t have joint pain or stiffness in other areas after repetitive tasks—most of my discomfort is just the progressively worsening pain in my left leg.”
